ug.headline: Uganda’s deputy speaker backs social protection law
ug.dek: Thomas Tayebwa says legislation should set rules for programmes and their financing, while partners seek higher grants for older people.
paragraphs: Uganda’s Deputy Speaker, Thomas Tayebwa, backed a proposal for a comprehensive social protection law during a meeting in Kampala on Thursday. The law would establish rules for implementing, coordinating and financing programmes for vulnerable people.

Tayebwa urged the Parliamentary Forum on Social Protection to work with the Executive, saying constitutional limits restrict private members’ bills that have financial implications for the Consolidated Fund. Development partners also called for the Senior Citizens Grant eligibility age to fall from 80 to 65 years and its monthly payment to rise from USh25,000 to USh35,000.

World Food Programme country representative Wanja Kaaria-Ndoho said approximately 10,000 older people received support in Karamoja in June during a recent drought. A second round was planned for approximately 17,000 additional older people across all nine districts; Tayebwa also commended advocacy for USh15 billion for the National Child Disability Assistance Programme.

ug.headline: Visa opens Kampala office as Uganda's central bank demands cheaper payments
ug.dek: Governor Michael Atingi-Ego also urged the company to help lenders assess small firms and strengthen protection against rising cybercrime.
paragraphs: Visa opened a Kampala office on November 26, and Bank of Uganda Governor Michael Atingi-Ego used the occasion to press the payments company to lower digital transaction costs, widen credit access for small businesses and improve cybersecurity. The office is meant to place Visa nearer to local banks, fintechs, businesses and regulators.

Atingi-Ego said micro, small and medium enterprises make up about 90% of private-sector businesses, yet only about one in 10 holds a formal loan or credit line. He urged Visa to apply its data analytics and artificial intelligence to help lenders judge firms that lack conventional credit records. Visa's Uganda country manager, Andrew Rugamba, said the company would first study the market and identify partners before announcing any collaborations.

Mobile money moved USh356 trillion in the year to June 2025, while roughly two-thirds of transactions in the economy are still made in cash. Visa plans to help two to three more Ugandan banks issue cards that work without an active internet connection over the coming year. Cybercrime cases reported to authorities rose from 245 in 2023 to 474 in 2024, then fell to 412 in 2025, Atingi-Ego said.

ug.dek: Founder Matthias Magoola says the company has more than 500 products and will launch six antimalarial medicines within two weeks.
paragraphs: Ugandan drugmaker Dei BioPharma is ready to supply medicines and vaccines across Africa, founder Matthias Magoola said at a public health conference in Addis Ababa on Wednesday. He said the company had more than 500 products available and needed a market for its manufacturing capacity.

Magoola said those products cover 70% to 80% of the molecules Africa imports. The company's campus in Matugga, Wakiso District, covers more than 400 acres, with more than 30 factories under development. He said it would make medicines from active ingredients through to finished products, using local raw materials such as cassava, maize, potatoes and sugarcane.

The company plans to launch six antimalarial medicines within two weeks, Magoola said, and has invited Africa CDC officials to the launch. He also said it had filed more than 100 patent applications in the United States, with more than 72 published.

ug.headline: Uganda wildlife board to review tourism revenue-sharing
ug.dek: Chairman James Kalema says the board will assess whether communities near protected areas benefit effectively from tourism income.
paragraphs: Uganda’s 11th Wildlife Authority Board of Trustees will review how tourism revenue-sharing benefits communities near protected areas, its chairman, Prof. James Kalema, said at its inauguration on Thursday, November 26. The board is also prioritising solutions to human-wildlife conflict and stronger action against poaching as it takes over oversight of the country’s wildlife resources.

Tourism, Wildlife and Antiquities Minister Col. Tom Butime inaugurated the board and urged it to ensure timely compensation for communities affected by wildlife. He said more than half of Uganda’s wildlife lives outside gazetted protected areas, making cooperation with communities important to conservation.

The board will also prepare the authority to manage additional protected areas and improve staff welfare. Kalema said visitor numbers had risen during the outgoing board’s tenure, but travel advisories linked to an Ebola outbreak in neighbouring Democratic Republic of Congo affected tourism as the peak season began.

ug.headline: Uganda and SANY Group agree to develop green investment proposals
ug.dek: The proposed work covers urban sanitation, recycling infrastructure and electric trucks, but the meeting produced no funding commitment or project timetable.
paragraphs: Ambassador Abbey Walusimbi, Uganda's senior presidential adviser on diaspora affairs, met representatives of the China-based SANY Group, a heavy-machinery and equipment maker, and Gogwa Corp, a Uganda-focused diaspora investment company operating from Sweden, at the President's Office in Kampala. They discussed investment in urban sanitation, waste management, recycling and electric mobility. The parties agreed to develop practical proposals, but announced no investment amount.

cv.headline: CV Interilhas asks Cape Verde to place two state ships in its concession
cv.dek: The operator says the concession contract requires changes to operating and financial models when new vessels are added.
paragraphs: Cape Verde’s maritime concessionaire CV Interilhas has asked the government to include two new state-owned ships, Djabraba and Nhô Eugénio Tavares, in its public maritime transport concession. The company sent its position on how to operate the vessels in a letter to Transport and Sea Minister João do Carmo Brito Soares, it said in a statement on Thursday.

CV Interilhas cited a 2023 amendment to the concession contract, which it says provides for new ships supplied by either the state or the company to join the concession. The clause also calls for adjustments to operating, economic and financial models, as well as the benchmarks used to calculate compensation, the operator said.

The company said the concession’s exclusivity terms could be undermined if the state made the vessels available to other private operators outside the contract and legal framework. It also cited public procurement and administrative contract rules.

cv.headline: ASSIMP demands Cape Verde restore prosecutor Nilton Moniz’s security
cv.dek: The prosecutors’ union contests the interior minister’s order to replace his personal protection gradually with other measures.
paragraphs: The Association of Public Prosecutors (ASSIMP) has demanded the immediate restoration of personal security for Nilton Moniz, a prosecutor in Cape Verde who handles complex cases, including Operation Shark, a probe into organised crime. The demand follows an order by the interior minister to withdraw his security and gradually replace it with other measures.

ASSIMP said the risk assessment behind the order rated the threat “moderate” and cited no concrete, current and corroborated threat. The union argues that preventive protection should not depend on a threat already materialising. The Superior Council of the Public Prosecution Service requested Moniz’s protection in 2025, and it remained in place for more than a year as his exposure increased, the union said.

ASSIMP also wants a technically qualified body to reassess the risk with the council involved, and has requested an urgent meeting with the minister. The union cited public disclosure that Moniz had charged the current prime minister, who leads the government responsible for the decision, and said the assessment must be impartial.

cv.headline: Cape Verde’s sea institute takes up fishing-device rules and emergency plan
cv.dek: IMar will present proposed rules for fish-aggregating devices and seek feedback on a maritime alert plan for artisanal fishing in Praia.
paragraphs: Cape Verde’s Institute of the Sea (IMar) will present proposed regulations for fish-aggregating devices at a workshop in Praia on 4 December. The institute will also discuss an emergency alert plan for rough seas affecting artisanal fishing.

IMar says experience with the devices has shown a need for clear rules to reduce disputes among fishing operators and manage marine resources. The plan is intended to improve prevention, alerts and risk management during extreme sea conditions and climate change, protecting fishers, coastal infrastructure and fishing communities.

The meeting at Hotel Vista, in Praia’s Achada Santo António area, will bring together public bodies, fishing groups, development partners and researchers to debate the proposals and offer changes. The work is part of a project implemented through an agreement between LuxDev and IMar.

cv.headline: Praia raises annual grants for three music groups to 750,000 escudos
cv.dek: The municipality raised Ferro Gaita's grant from 500,000 escudos and extended the same annual support to Bulimundo and Os Tubarões.
paragraphs: Praia's municipal government has raised its annual grant to Ferro Gaita to 750,000 escudos and extended the same support to Bulimundo and Os Tubarões. Mayor Fernando Pinto signed the agreement with representatives of the three bands, Estevão "Iduino" Tavares for Ferro Gaita, Jorge Lima for Os Tubarões and Silvestre "Silva" Alfama for Bulimundo.

Pinto said the funding recognises the groups' long history and contribution to Cape Verdean culture. He said the support should help them train young people and promote traditional music at home and abroad, and he called for new traditional music projects to emerge. The representatives thanked the council and said the grant would be essential to keep their activities going.
The ceremony also paid tribute to Bino Branco, known as the "man of the ferrinho", a figure in Ferro Gaita's history.

td.headline: Chad's justice ministry orders prosecutors to stop police custody in civil disputes
td.dek: A 25 November circular tells prosecutors general to summon judicial police officers and enforce the ban on custody in civil, commercial and social cases.
paragraphs: Chad's Ministry of Justice has ordered prosecutors general to enforce a strict ban on judicial police handling civil, commercial and social disputes or using custody in those cases. Justice and Human Rights Minister Ndolenodji Alixe Naimbaye issued the circular on 25 November 2026.

The ministry said abuses persist in police stations and gendarmerie brigades despite earlier circulars in 2023 and January 2026. Prosecutors general are to summon every judicial police officer in their territory and formally forbid custody and interference in such disputes.
The ministry also told judicial authorities to apply law No. 011/AN-SENAT/2025, amending the rules, with the prohibition enforced in full rigour.

dj.headline: Djibouti's parliament to review 12 public bodies' 2025 accounts
dj.dek: The texts cover energy, water, pensions, employment, broadcasting and other state bodies under parliamentary oversight of public funds.
paragraphs: Djibouti's National Assembly will review the 2025 accounts of 12 public bodies in plenary on Wednesday, 2 December, after the Conference of Presidents approved the committees' work programme. The accounts cover state bodies in energy, water, regulation, employment, pensions, broadcasting, property, construction, judicial studies and public facilities.

The meeting was chaired by Assembly President Dileita Mohamed Dileita and attended by Prime Minister Abdoulkader Kamil Mohamed, with Justice Minister Ali Hassan Bahdon for the government, according to the Djiboutian Information Agency. The review is part of parliament's annual oversight of public funds and lets lawmakers examine the results of bodies under state supervision.

The accounts include those of the Djiboutian Hydrocarbons Company, the national water and sanitation office and Radio Television Djibouti. Lawmakers will examine them in committee before the plenary session.

paragraphs: Eswatini's Cabinet has approved a judicial inquiry into corruption, Agriculture Minister Mandla Tshawuka said at an editors' forum in Mbabane. Parliament recently passed the motion calling for the investigation.

sz.headline: Eswatini secures air cargo licence as security compliance reaches 85%
sz.dek: Principal Secretary Thulani Mkhaliphi said the licence was obtained in the week before he spoke, after the country raised aviation security compliance from about 35%.
paragraphs: Eswatini has secured an air cargo carrying licence after improving its aviation security compliance from about 35% to around 85%, Principal Secretary Thulani Mkhaliphi said. The licence followed progress in meeting regulatory requirements for the country's aviation operations.

Mkhaliphi announced the licence at a Swaziland Editors Forum open forum on development financing and debt sustainability at the Mountain View hotel in Mbabane on Thursday. He said reaching this stage took considerable time because several aspects of aviation operations had to be aligned with required standards. International aviation players were taking notice of the country's progress, he said.

Mkhaliphi also said Eswatini should not let its lack of a coastline keep it from maritime trade, noting that about 80% of international trade moves by sea. The Ministry of Public Works and Transport is also developing a QR code system so transport inspectors can verify public transport permits electronically.

sz.headline: Eswatini soldiers walk in support of national HIV response
sz.dek: The defence force held the solidarity walk from Matsapha to Nokwane Headquarters on 26 November, urging testing and continued treatment.
paragraphs: Soldiers from the Umbutfo Eswatini Defence Force walked from Matsapha to Nokwane Headquarters on 26 November in support of Eswatini’s national response to HIV/AIDS. Participants also lit a candle during the solidarity event.

The force said it supports people living with HIV and promotes adherence to treatment. Director of the National Emergency Response Council on HIV and AIDS Nondumiso Mncube and Health Ministry administrator Cebile Dlamini attended, along with military officers and representatives of health and emergency services. The force provides integrated HIV, tuberculosis and other high-burden disease services in its barracks.

Organisers reported declines in HIV- and TB-related deaths and said AIDS-related deaths had been nearly eliminated. They urged people who do not know their HIV status to get tested and said prevention, treatment adherence and support for people who test positive remain priorities.

ga.headline: Cimaf-Gabon lifts cement capacity to 1,85 million tonnes
ga.dek: The 25 milliards de francs CFA investment adds one million tonnes of annual capacity before Gabon’s planned clinker import ban.
paragraphs: Cimaf-Gabon inaugurated its third cement production line in Owendo on 26 novembre, taking the company’s annual production capacity from 850 000 to 1,85 million tonnes. President Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema opened the line.

The 25 milliards de francs CFA investment adds one million tonnes of capacity. Authorities said the expansion is intended to meet demand from road, property and infrastructure projects and reduce reliance on imports. Cimaf-Gabon’s activity now accounts for nearly 1,000 direct and indirect jobs.
The new line comes before the planned 1er janvier 2027 ban on clinker imports, a raw material used to make cement. The investment was made under an agreement with the Gabonese state.

ga.headline: Gabon receives 37 600 chicks for poultry farmers
ga.dek: The second delivery brings the total received to 75 200, with 262 400 expected by 17 December for 79 farmers across eight provinces.
paragraphs: Gabon received a second shipment of 37 600 day-old chicks at Libreville’s Léon-Mba International Airport on 25 November, under its emergency poultry plan. The chicks are intended for domestic broiler production ahead of a ban on broiler imports scheduled for 1 January 2027.

The Agriculture Ministry said the delivery brings the number received since the programme began on 19 November to 75 200. A total of 262 400 chicks are expected by 17 December for 79 farmers in the country’s eight provinces. The state is covering feed and veterinary products for this first phase.

Agriculture Minister Pacôme Kossy said the plan targets nearly 500 tonnes of locally produced broiler meat for the year-end holidays. Gabon imports about 55 000 tonnes annually, according to the report.

ga.headline: Gabon seeks Rwanda's help to train young agricultural entrepreneurs
ga.dek: Vice-President Alexandre Barro Chambrier asked Paul Kagame for expertise as Gabon pursues a new agricultural model by 2030.
paragraphs: Gabon's Vice-President Alexandre Barro Chambrier asked Rwanda to help train and support young entrepreneurs, particularly in agriculture, during a meeting with President Paul Kagame in Kigali on 25 November. The talks covered food sovereignty, digital cooperation and trade, as Libreville looks to Rwanda's experience for its economic transformation.

Barro Chambrier presented Gabon's national entrepreneurship support instruments, including the Gabonese Export Credit Bank (BCEG), the Support Fund for Micro-Enterprises (FAMAD) and the "Help me help you" programme. Gabon wants to build a new agricultural model by 2030 and is seeking Rwanda's experience in training young entrepreneurs.

The meeting took place alongside the YouthConnekt Africa summit, which runs in Kigali from 25 to 27 November. 80 Gabonese young entrepreneurs are attending to present projects and seek financing and partnerships; the two countries also agreed to strengthen trade and cooperation in digital services and entrepreneur mobility.

ga.headline: Gabon seeks rules for traditional medicine practitioners
ga.dek: A Libreville workshop is examining draft rules on practice, recognition and treatment centres, with a roadmap due by 27 November.
paragraphs: Gabon’s health ministry opened a national workshop in Libreville on 25 November to set a legal and institutional framework for traditional medicine. Participants are to examine draft rules on how practitioners work, how they are recognised and how traditional treatment centres operate.

Health Minister Elsa Nkana Joséphine Ayo épouse Bivigou said the practice had operated outside the formal health system without sufficiently structured safeguards for quality, safety and institutional recognition. The proposals also cover a national council for traditional medicine, permits to practise and the classification of traditional medicines.

The workshop runs through 27 November. Participants are expected to produce a roadmap, a working method and tools to monitor implementation. The government says the framework will support cooperation between traditional practitioners, researchers and health professionals under standards for safety, effectiveness and medical ethics.

ga.headline: Gabon's interior minister orders police crackdown on Libreville crime
ga.dek: Edgar Moukoumbi met national police command to launch operations targeting racketeering, illegal immigration and traffic congestion in the capital.
paragraphs: Gabon's Interior Minister Edgar Moukoumbi convened the national police high command on November 25 to implement a new government security roadmap. The meeting aimed to define operational methods for protecting people and property across Libreville.

Moukoumbi directed police to combat illegal immigration, racketeering, noise pollution, traffic congestion and general insecurity. He also ordered action against unregistered places of worship and self-proclaimed religious preachers. Police Chief Serge Hervé Ngoma led the command staff during the session.

Before the police briefing, Moukoumbi discussed security cooperation with Turkish diplomat Can Incesu. Ankara expressed willingness to strengthen bilateral ties in strategic sectors. The ministry now faces pressure to translate these directives into visible results for residents.

gm.headline: Gambia's central bank holds policy rate at 14% as inflation rises
gm.dek: The Monetary Policy Committee kept three other rates unchanged after inflation climbed to 6.3% in October, ending three months of declines.
paragraphs: The Central Bank of The Gambia kept its Monetary Policy Rate at 14% after a two-day Monetary Policy Committee meeting on November 25 and 26, as annual headline inflation rose to 6.3% in October from 6.1% in September.

Governor Buah Saidy announced the decision at a press briefing. The bank also left the Required Reserve Ratio at 13%, its lending facility rate at 15% and its deposit facility rate at 5%. Food inflation reached 5.4%, while non-food inflation held at 7.6%.

The bank forecasts inflation will average 6.4% in 2026 and move toward its 5% medium-term target in 2027. It projects economic growth of 5.5% this year, 0.3 percentage points below its August forecast.

gm.headline: ECOWAS gives Gambia election bodies US$480,000 for December poll
gm.dek: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is funding training for polling staff and civil society groups ahead of the December 5 presidential election.
paragraphs: The Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) has provided US$480,000 to support The Gambia's December 5 presidential election. Namizata Meite Sangare, the bloc's resident representative and head of mission in The Gambia, presented the cheques in Banjul on November 25.

The Independent Electoral Commission will use its share to train 8,851 polling staff, its chairman Joseph Colley said. Recipients also include the National Human Rights Commission, the Gambia Bar Association and the Gambia Press Union. The Gambian chapter of the Inter-Africa Network for Women, Media, Gender and Development (FAMEDEV) said its grant would fund a women-led election observatory and an early warning mechanism to help prevent conflict.

ECOWAS has had long-term election observers in The Gambia since November 10, and short-term observers are expected before polling day. Serigne Ka, the bloc's head of electoral assistance, said the support also includes training on tabulating and transmitting results, and voter education.

gm.headline: Gambia's Alliance of Progressive Citizens joins UDP-led coalition before presidential vote
gm.dek: Lamin Sima signed a memorandum of understanding in Jarra Soma, aligning his party with the United Democratic Party (UDP) alliance behind Ousainou Darboe.
paragraphs: The Alliance of Progressive Citizens (APC), led by Lamin Sima, joined the Gambia First Coalition (GFC) at a signing ceremony at the UDP bureau in Jarra Soma on 26 November. The UDP-led alliance has endorsed lawyer Ousainou Darboe as its flagbearer for the 5 December presidential election.

Sima, who withdrew from the presidential race, is the second cleared candidate to leave the contest and join the coalition. He said the APC's decision was unanimous and followed consultations that included Gambians in the diaspora, and that party supporters would campaign alongside GFC and UDP partners. The coalition now comprises 11 political parties and seven political movements.
Darboe welcomed APC's entry and urged alliance partners to work collectively and strengthen outreach. Recent polls indicate that incumbent President Adama Barrow holds only a narrow lead.

gm.headline: Bensouda pledges separate Area Council and university for Foni
gm.dek: The Unite Party leader and coalition presidential candidate says the changes would bring administration closer to residents and keep young people in the region for tertiary.
paragraphs: Talib Ahmed Bensouda, leader of the Unite Party (UNITE) and flagbearer of the Unite Coalition 2026, pledged during a campaign tour of Foni to establish the region as a separate Area Council or administrative area and build a university there. He made the promises in Foni Bondali, saying residents deserved greater administrative recognition and development attention.

Bensouda said a separate council would bring governance closer to communities and improve services. He said young people should be able to pursue tertiary education in Foni rather than travel elsewhere. He also pledged to improve healthcare, pointing to Bondali Hospital's limited maternity facilities, including one maternity bed in a large ward.

He criticised President Adama Barrow's administration over irregular migration, linking it to unemployment, poverty and poor leadership, and promised more jobs for young people. Bensouda also pledged better salaries and living conditions for public-sector workers and informal traders.

gn.headline: Guinea raises monthly sanitation budget for Conakry communes to 15 billion francs
gn.dek: The minister puts the real monthly cost at 23 billion francs for Conakry and 109 billion nationwide, against the old 3 billion to 3.5 billion.
paragraphs: Guinea's government has raised the monthly sanitation budget for the communes of Grand Conakry to 15 billion Guinean francs, the Prime Minister Amadou Oury Bah announced at a sanitation forum in Conakry on November 25 and 26. The minister of sanitation, Aboubacar Camara, said the new sum has not yet been disbursed and that payment for this month is still awaited.

Before the Dar Es Salam landfill closed in October, all of Conakry's communes together received between 3 billion and 3.5 billion francs a month, Camara said. Dividing that across 13 communes left about 7 million francs a day for each, he added, while the real monthly cost is 23 billion francs for Conakry alone and 109 billion francs nationwide.

The forum aimed to find lasting funding mechanisms for keeping the capital and interior cities clean. Bah urged local elected officials to make the capital clean by the end of the year, and the government plans a polluter-pays tax from 2027.

gn.headline: Guinea minister calls for action as 94.7% of women face genital mutilation
gn.dek: Aminata Kaba urged families and institutions to protect survivors and end impunity during the national campaign running from 25 November to 10 December.
paragraphs: Guinea’s minister for women, family and solidarity, Aminata Kaba, called for national action against violence toward women and girls as a 16-day campaign began on 25 November. It runs through 10 December and sets out priorities of access to justice, survivor protection and ending impunity.

National data cited by the ministry show that 94.7% of women aged 15 to 49 have experienced female genital mutilation. The figures also say 80.7% of women aged 15 to 69 have faced at least one form of violence in their lives, while about 46% of girls marry before age 18.

Kaba called on parents and families to listen to children and protect women and girls, and urged families to keep girls in school. She said state bodies, communities, religious and traditional leaders, media, civil society and the private sector all share responsibility for addressing the violence.

gn.headline: Conakry Terminal secures €82.6 million loan to extend port quays
gn.dek: AFG Bank and Ecobank will finance the next phase of Quai 14 at the Port of Conakry, part of a €341 million investment in quay capacity.
paragraphs: Conakry Terminal, a subsidiary of the AGL group, signed a €82.6 million financing agreement with AFG Bank and Ecobank on 26 November to develop additional quays at the Port of Conakry. The funding goes to the Quai 14 project.

The terminal said €85.2 million of the project's €341 million total had already been mobilised and pre-financed from its own funds. The new agreement finances the next phase, which the terminal says will expand operating capacity and improve the flow of port operations.

The terminal has also started studies for Quai 16, which would add 400 metres of quay and require nearly €400 million in further investment. It said the expansion is meant to prepare for volumes from projects under the Simandou 2040 programme.

gn.headline: Guinea fonio project sets processing standard and supports six firms
gn.dek: The programme, backed by the Netherlands and running since 2023, trained businesses and linked them with investors and international markets.
paragraphs: A Guinea fonio programme supported by the Dutch government formally closed in Conakry on Thursday, 26 November, ahead of its planned end in December 2026. Since 2023, it has worked with six small and medium-sized businesses and national institutions to improve production and processing.

Project lead Femke Dekker said the programme produced good-practice manuals, established a standard for precooked fonio and helped the six firms prepare food-safety and social-responsibility action plans. The businesses also received training in food safety, organic certification and packaging, and introductions to investors and international markets.

Sira Bayo, head of Guinea’s fonio industry body, said the support helped producers and processors adopt standards and better production practices. She said stronger equipment is needed to increase processing capacity.

gn.headline: Guinea's labour minister takes lead of African labour administration centre
gn.dek: Ramatoulaye Camara was elected board president for one year at the 45th ordinary session in Conakry, while another Guinean official was named to head the centre for three years.
paragraphs: Guinea's minister of employment, labour and social protection, Ramatoulaye Camara, was elected to a one-year term as president of the board of the African Regional Centre for Labour Administration (CRADAT), an intergovernmental body, at the close of its 45th ordinary session in Conakry on Thursday, November 26. Another Guinean official takes over as director-general for three years.

Representatives of the centre's 18 member states took part in the session. Camara said a selection committee reviewed the applications from Gabon, Togo and Guinea before choosing the Guinean candidate. She described the appointments as the first time two women from Guinea hold the centre's top posts: herself as board president, and a labour inspector and magistrate as director-general.

The outgoing board president, Justin Cyprien Ilboudo of Burkina Faso, said the centre trains, advises and researches labour administration across its member states. Guinea's prime minister, Amadou Oury Bah, said changes in the labour market, including artificial intelligence, are raising demand for specialist skills.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau sets presidential and legislative elections for 2028
gw.dek: Transition President Horta Inta-a cited missing technical, material and financial conditions for the vote, originally scheduled for 6 December 2026.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau’s transition president, Horta Inta-a, has set 26 November 2028 for presidential and legislative elections, postponing the vote originally scheduled for 6 December 2026. The date is in Presidential Decree No. 35/2026, released on 26 November by the presidency’s communications office.

The decree says the country lacks the technical, material and financial conditions needed to hold the elections. It warns that voting without meeting legal, technical and operational requirements could undermine the process’s regularity, transparency, inclusion and credibility, as well as public and political actors’ confidence.

The decree calls for the electoral calendar to be reviewed with the relevant institutions and other participants. It also says the authorities should advance the establishment of local governments through the first municipal elections provided for in the transition political charter and applicable law.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau delays presidential and parliamentary elections until 2028
gw.dek: A decree moves the vote from 6 December to 26 November 2028 after the presidency said election preparations lacked sufficient resources.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau’s transitional president, Gen Horta N’Tam, has postponed presidential and parliamentary elections from 6 December to 26 November 2028, delaying the planned return to civilian rule by two years.

The presidency said an assessment found insufficient technical, material and financial conditions to hold the polls as scheduled. It said the extra time would help ensure credible, transparent and inclusive elections, with equal opportunities for all candidates.

The announcement came a year after the military seized power and promised a return to civilian rule within 12 months. The presidency reiterated its commitment to the country’s first local government elections but set no date for them.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau parties demand election calendar a year after coup
gw.dek: The government and electoral commission postponed the vote planned for 6 December 2026, citing a lack of technical and logistical conditions.
paragraphs: Guinea-Bissau’s political parties are demanding an election calendar a year after a military takeover halted the vote-counting process and installed a transitional government. The attempt to seize power came on 26 November 2025, three days after presidential and parliamentary elections.

The military announced it was taking power while the country awaited results, suspended the election process and removed President Umaro Sissoco Embaló. The government and National Electoral Commission later postponed the vote intended to end the transition, which had been scheduled for 6 December 2026, saying technical and logistical conditions were lacking.

During the transition, authorities held a constitutional referendum boycotted by the main opposition parties. The new constitution strengthened presidential powers and changed rules for diaspora participation in elections.

gw.headline: Guinea-Bissau hospital offers free prostate screening on two dates
gw.dek: The National Simão Mendes Hospital is providing consultations and screening tests to the public and health workers as part of Novembro Azul.
paragraphs: The National Simão Mendes Hospital (HNSM), Guinea-Bissau’s largest hospital, opened its Novembro Azul campaign on 26 November 2026, urging stronger prevention and early diagnosis of prostate cancer. The hospital is offering free consultations and screening tests to the public and its own workers.

Doctor Delfim Cabral said early detection improves the chances of effective treatment and control. The campaign also includes scientific talks to strengthen health workers’ skills in prevention, screening and patient follow-up.

Free consultations and prostate-specific antigen (PSA) tests were scheduled for 27 November and 01 December, according to Conosaba do Porto. Cabral also urged community leaders, civil society groups, media and families to share clear information and challenge myths about the disease.

lr.headline: Liberia's Senate orders probe into cash shortage and high prices
lr.dek: The inquiry follows complaints that banknotes remain scarce and essential goods costly despite the local currency's appreciation to about L$163 per US$1.
paragraphs: Liberia’s Senate has ordered its Joint Committees on Banking and Currency and Public Accounts to investigate shortages of Liberian dollar banknotes and rising prices of basic commodities. The decision followed concerns raised by River Gee County Senator Jonathan Sogbie during a Senate session on Thursday, November 26.

Sogbie said the Senate authorized the Central Bank of Liberia to procure and print up to L$79 billion on July 16, but banks and markets still lack usable notes. The Central Bank puts the exchange rate at about L$163 to US$1. Consumers say the currency’s appreciation has not brought lower prices for essential goods.
Sogbie said households rely on annual Susu savings clubs for Christmas and end-of-year expenses, and urged monetary authorities to explain why prices remain high.

lr.headline: Liberia's agriculture minister warns El Niño could cut rice yields by up to 50%
lr.dek: Dr. J. Alexander Nuetah told lawmakers severe conditions could reduce yields by 30 to 50% for crops planted during the affected period.
paragraphs: Liberia’s agriculture minister, Dr. J. Alexander Nuetah, warned lawmakers that potential El Niño conditions could disrupt planting schedules and cut rice yields by 30 to 50% for crops planted during the affected period. He spoke alongside Environmental Protection Agency Executive Director Dr. Emmanuel Urey Yarkpawolo at the House of Representatives.

Nuetah said failed rains after farmers plant in March could destroy crops, while excessive rain could rot seeds before they germinate. He said rice varieties need 90 to 150 days to mature, and shorter rainy seasons could leave long-cycle plants without enough water during flowering and grain formation.

The officials also warned that intense heat could hinder germination and increase pests, while heavy rain could flood swamp rice fields. Nuetah said these risks could threaten food security in rural communities dependent on rice.

lr.headline: Boakai ties Liberia’s US$5.7 billion infrastructure plan to future gold revenue
lr.dek: The agreement with Bea Mountain Mining Corporation covers four power plants, a transmission network and 14 road and bridge projects over five years.
paragraphs: Liberian President Joseph Nyuma Boakai signed a US$5.7 billion agreement with Bea Mountain Mining Corporation on Wednesday to build four power plants, a national transmission network and 14 road and bridge projects within five years. The government says it will finance the work with new revenue from the mining company beginning in 2027, rather than cash up front.

The agreement provides for 270 megawatts of additional electricity and a 146-kilometer highway. The company also agreed to a US$500 million bridge financing facility, according to FrontPage Africa. Boakai said the government would set aside the new revenue streams to fund the projects.

Alexander B. Cummings, political leader of the opposition Alternative National Congress, questioned the price of the deal at a news conference Thursday, warning that future generations could bear the cost. The government insists the agreement adds no borrowing.

lr.headline: Liberia deploys 285 road machines across 15 counties
lr.dek: The equipment is stationed at 19 hubs, but the initiative's lasting value will depend on maintenance, budgets and public reporting.
paragraphs: Liberia has deployed 285 pieces of earth-moving and support equipment across all 15 counties, using 19 operational hubs to tackle poor roads. The nationwide rollout gives public works authorities machinery to rehabilitate roads, including in rural communities.

The report by journalist Evelyn Kpadeh Seagbeh says the machines need trained operators and mechanics, servicing and spare-parts budgets, secure storage and regular performance checks. It calls for public reporting on where equipment is deployed, which roads are repaired and whether machines remain operational.
The report says results should be judged by passable road kilometres, communities connected, transport costs and access to services, as well as how many machines still work five or 10 years later.

lr.headline: Liberia’s petroleum regulator sets 2027 deadline for first sector report
lr.dek: The five-year plan also follows the authority’s report of US$13.8 million in contributions to the national budget over three years.
paragraphs: Liberia’s Petroleum Regulatory Authority (LPRA) unveiled a five-year plan covering 2026 to 2030 on Thursday in Monrovia, committing to publish its first State of the Petroleum Sector Report in 2027. Director General Marilyn T. Logan presented the plan at the Ellen Johnson Sirleaf Ministerial Complex.

Logan said the authority contributed US$13.8 million to Liberia’s national budget over the past three years and now ranks among the country’s 11 highest revenue contributors. She also said the legislature ratified all eight production-sharing contracts secured and signed by the LPRA within 18 months of the current leadership taking office in March 2024.
A reconnaissance programme is underway in the Harper Basin. The LPRA’s 2026 Direct Negotiation Licensing Round, launched last month, is expected to exceed the results achieved in 2025.

ly.headline: Libya's Abdelaziz urges 10-year school reform amid teachers' strike
ly.dek: He argues the sector employs far more people than it needs, pointing to 700,000 staff and teachers against 1.3 million students.
paragraphs: Mahmoud Abdelaziz has criticised the teachers' strike now under way in Libya, saying it is disrupting the academic year and has gone beyond acceptable limits. He also rejected a union proposal to make up missed lessons on Fridays and Saturdays.

Abdelaziz put the number of education staff and teachers at more than 700,000, against 1.3 million students, and said Libya needs no more than 150,000 teachers, citing scientific data. He called for a 10-year plan to reform the sector, insisting that any cut should not leave employees without income, and said a bigger education budget alone would not fix the imbalance.

He said hundreds of thousands were hired with salaries of 150 to 160 dinars, and that many appointments made in and before 2011 should never have been made. He added that paying all outstanding wages at once is unrealistic, and that weekends should stay free for students.

ly.headline: Libya's oil corporation sets gas output and flaring goals at Tripoli panels
ly.dek: At the Libya Energy 2026 conference (LIBYES 2026), participants discussed raising production to 4 billion cubic feet per day and ending routine flaring by 2030.
paragraphs: Libya's National Oil Corporation (NOC) plans to increase gas production to 4 billion cubic feet per day, according to discussions on the second day of the Libya Energy 2026 conference (LIBYES 2026) in Tripoli. The event ran from 24 to 26 November, and its gas panels examined domestic supply and regional exports.

The first panel covered infrastructure, reducing flaring, meeting domestic demand, supporting local industries and supplying power generation. A second panel brought together participants from the NOC, Mellitah Oil & Gas and Nafusah Oil Operations to discuss ending routine flaring and turning gas into added value.

Their proposed measures included pipelines and compressors, gas reinjection, power generation, and compressed natural gas and liquefied natural gas technologies. Participants discussed a goal of zero routine flaring by 2030, and local and international organisations, companies, researchers and energy ministry delegates attended.

ly.headline: Libya's investment authority and state oil company sign deal with Oman's OQ partner
ly.dek: The agreement, signed in Tripoli, starts preliminary legal steps to explore oil and gas investment opportunities among the three parties.
paragraphs: Libya's Investment Authority (LIA), Oman's OQ Exploration and Production (OQEP) and the National Oil Corporation (NOC) signed an agreement in Tripoli on November 24 to explore investment opportunities in the oil and gas sector. The signing took place during the LIBYES 2026 event, held from November 24 to 26.

The LIA said the agreement begins preliminary legal procedures for work with the National Oil Corporation. It sets up a framework for cooperation and the exchange of expertise, drawing on the parties' technical and investment capabilities.

The agreement implements a memorandum of understanding between the LIA and Oman's OQ group signed earlier this year. The LIA said it aims to grow the value of its assets through partnerships that benefit Libya's economy.

ly.headline: Libya agrees visit to assess border surveillance towers
ly.dek: The Customs Authority and the European Union mission will inspect sites near Tunisia and discuss repairs, equipment and a proposed joint monitoring centre.
paragraphs: Libya’s Customs Authority agreed on 25 November to coordinate a field visit to surveillance towers in the Al-Assa area, near the Tunisian border, after meeting the European Union Border Assistance Mission (EUBAM) at its Tripoli headquarters. The talks covered cooperation on land and sea border monitoring.

The Customs Authority said the visit will assess the condition of the Bal-Sharaf, Tawilat al-Rutba and Al-Quradiyah towers and identify maintenance and equipment needs. Work on maintenance and camera installation at Bal-Sharaf has already been completed. The meeting was chaired by Major General Al-Tahir Khair, director of the Land Border Surveillance Department.

Officials also discussed specialist training for border personnel and a proposal for a joint surveillance centre involving the Customs Authority and the interior and defence ministries. They raised equipment and logistical needs at the Wazin crossing and the Nalut surveillance unit.

mg.headline: Madagascar targets 5.1% growth in 2027 budget
mg.dek: The plan raises public spending by 11% and relies on higher tax and customs receipts to finance 24 priority programmes.
paragraphs: Madagascar’s government is forecasting 5.1% economic growth in 2027, up from an estimated 4.1% in 2026, under its draft initial finance law presented to lawmakers in Tsimbazaza. The plan also proposes an 11% rise in public spending and increased taxes on some goods.

Finance Minister Herinjatovo Aimé Ramiarison presented the budget proposal. It projects tax and customs revenue of 13 503,2 billion ariary and spending of 19 374,2 billion ariary. Proposed measures include a 30% customs duty on some luxury goods, harmful products and imports competing with local production, and a diesel tax of 503 ariary per litre, matching the tax on super petrol.

The government expects inflation to rise from 8.2% in 2026 to 8.3% in 2027. Its 24 priority programmes focus on sectors including agriculture, tourism, textiles and telecommunications; the proposal also sets aside support for Jirama, the state power and water company.

mg.headline: Madagascar elects Marco Tsaradia as Assembly president with 129 votes
mg.dek: The former supporter of Andry Rajoelina won unopposed after other candidates withdrew and Firaisankina deputies left the chamber.
paragraphs: Madagascar’s National Assembly elected Marco Tsaradia as its president on Wednesday, 25 November, with 129 votes from 130 lawmakers who voted. Tsaradia, a deputy from Ampanihy, succeeds Siteny Randrianasoloniaiko, who was removed from the post on Monday.

Tsaradia was the only candidate at the vote after several lawmakers withdrew their bids. Deputies from Firaisankina, a parliamentary group led by Fidèle Razara Piera, left the chamber before voting. Randrianasoloniaiko did not take part.

Tsaradia had supported former president Andry Rajoelina before the political changes of October 2026 and has since aligned with supporters of the current government. He leads the VFM, a platform made up mainly of deputies formerly aligned with Rajoelina.

mg.headline: Madagascar’s armed forces receive 12 drones and qualify 17 military personnel
mg.dek: The two-week course included 70 flight hours, with the armed forces expected to train future pilots independently.
paragraphs: Madagascar’s armed forces received 12 drones and qualified 17 military personnel after a two-week course at Manjakandriana. The group comprised 11 instructors and six drone pilots from different units; the handover took place at a ceremony attended by a representative of the Army chief of staff.

The trainees logged 70 flight hours, with one week focused on technical skills and the other on tactical use. The aircraft are DJI Matrice 4 models, and the armed forces’ joint operations centre director, General Herisoa Mario Rakotomalala, said they would support troops in the field and help commanders make decisions.

French instructor Corporal Dylan said the goal was for Madagascar’s armed forces to run future training independently. The handover was part of military instruction by France’s Forces in the Southern Indian Ocean zone; a separate technical training detachment also served Madagascar’s navy in Diego.

mg.headline: Edenia takes Malagasy chocolate to Paris-area Christmas fair
mg.dek: The Madagascar craft chocolatier plans to show about 15 products at the 19 December event organised by ASASOA France-Madagascar.
paragraphs: Edenia Chocolaterie Madagascar will exhibit at the second Foire de Noël Art et Gastronomie on 19 December at the Ferme du Manet in Montigny-le-Bretonneux, near Paris. The Malagasy craft chocolatier plans to bring a quince of references and nearly 40 kilos of chocolate.

Founder Achille Rajerison is due to fly to France from 30 November to prepare for the fair, organised by ASASOA France-Madagascar. Edenia’s recipes pair Malagasy cacao with vanilla, combava, wild tsiperifery pepper, lychee and cinnamon; the company grows some ingredients, including lychee and cinnamon, at Soatanana in Vatomandry district.
Rajerison said the fair would let the company present its products and meet the Malagasy diaspora. Edenia has already formed several partnerships in France, according to Midi Madagasikara.

mw.headline: Malawi’s black-market dollar reaches K5,000 as official rate holds at K1,751
mw.dek: Spot checks in major cities found vendors buying dollars for K4,500 to K4,700 and selling them for K5,000.
paragraphs: The US dollar was selling for K5,000 on Malawi’s parallel market, while the official exchange rate remained at K1,751, Nyasa Times reported Friday. The widening gap leaves buyers paying far more through unauthorised vendors than at official institutions.

Spot checks in major cities found vendors buying dollars for between K4,500 and K4,700 before reselling them at K5,000. One forex dealer said he bought $3,000 from Tanzanian merchandise sellers at K4,550 each on Wednesday.
The dealer said customers seeking dollars from him would have to pay K5,000 per dollar.

mw.headline: ESCOM prepares mass disconnections over K77 billion in unpaid bills
mw.dek: Government ministries and agencies account for more than half of the power utility’s approximately K77 billion debt, officials told Parliament.
paragraphs: Malawi’s Electricity Supply Corporation (ESCOM) is preparing to disconnect customers with unpaid bills after government ministries, departments and agencies were found to account for more than half of the approximately K77 billion owed to the utility. ESCOM officials disclosed the debt to Parliament’s Committee on Commissions, Statutory Corporations and State Enterprises.

Acting Finance Director Lawson Nakoma said notices had been sent to affected institutions. Debtors include Blantyre, Lilongwe and Northern Region water boards, State Residences, the Ministry of Health and Salima Sugar Company. Water boards are among the institutions with some of the highest outstanding debts.
The notices put the affected institutions on notice of disconnection as ESCOM seeks payment of the overdue bills.

mw.headline: Malawi's doctors' union calls for health-sector emergency
mw.dek: Shortages of medicines, fuel and staff have left public hospitals unable to deliver essential care, the union says.
paragraphs: The Medical Doctors Union of Malawi (MDUM) wants the government to declare a national emergency in the health sector, pointing to shortages of medicines, medical supplies, fuel, protective equipment and healthcare workers. In a statement dated November 26, 2026, titled "A Health System on Its Knees", the union said public hospitals are finding it hard to keep essential services running.

Some ambulances have been grounded for lack of fuel, leaving patients stranded when they need urgent care. MDUM cited a mother who reportedly died with her stillborn baby at Mponela Rural Hospital after two functional ambulances were grounded by fuel shortages. It also said a man from Thandaza Village in Traditional Authority Kasakula, Ntchisi District, died on October 20, 2026, while walking about 25 kilometres in search of medical attention.
The union warned that more lives could be lost unless the government moves quickly to restore essential health services.

mw.headline: Malawi’s MAIIC sets seven-day deadline for K55 billion farm loan recovery
mw.dek: The corporation will take defaulters to court if they do not pay after a final demand notice, and may seek to sell their assets.
paragraphs: Malawi Agricultural and Industrial Investment Corporation (MAIIC) will give beneficiaries of the government’s Mega Farms Initiative a final seven-day demand to settle unpaid loans totalling K55 billion before starting court proceedings. The repayment deadline, which required farmers to deliver maize to designated depots, expired on November 22, 2026.

MAIIC Managing Director Taz Chaponda said some beneficiaries had delivered maize, while others had not met their obligations. Those in default will be referred to the corporation’s external legal counsel for formal notices, he said.

Chaponda said cases could proceed through summary judgment or full court hearings. If beneficiaries fail to meet court judgments, MAIIC may seek asset attachment and sale, garnishee orders or other permitted recovery measures.

mw.headline: Malawi blocks film premiere at Lilongwe convention centre
mw.dek: The government cited the censorship law, while the production company says the film had been submitted for review on November 23.
paragraphs: Malawi’s government blocked the Friday premiere of State of the National Address, a locally produced film, at the Bingu International Convention Centre in Lilongwe. The film’s producer, 4Kaya Films Inc, said organisers were told the event could not proceed under the Censorship and Control of Entertainment Act.

4Kaya director Ezaius Mkandawire said the company sent the film to authorities on November 23 and was asked only to add end credits naming those involved. The company said the government had approved filming locations and received a copy for review. Arts Director Humphrey Mpondaminga said organisers had not followed procedures.

4Kaya said it would refund tickets in full and called for a review of Malawi’s censorship laws, which it described as outdated and inconsistent with democratic values and the creative industry’s growth.

ml.headline: Mali approves state transport and logistics company
ml.dek: The National Transition Council ratified the law establishing the SMTL, which is tasked with freight, passenger transport and logistics facilities.
paragraphs: Mali’s National Transition Council ratified a law on Thursday, 26 November, establishing the Malian Transport and Logistics Company (SMTL), a state-owned operator. The bill received 117 votes in favour, none against and one abstention.

Transport Minister Dembélé Madina Sissoko presented the measure. The company is authorised to support imports and exports, carry passengers and freight within Mali, and develop storage and other logistics facilities, including for fuel, agricultural inputs and food.
The government says the SMTL will complement private transport operators. Its creation was set out in an ordinance dated 29 September 2026, now ratified by the council.

ml.headline: Power cuts persist in Mali’s Douentza and Macina despite Bamako improvement
ml.dek: Fuel shortages have plunged Douentza into darkness since Monday, forcing artisans to spend more on diesel generators while food sellers lose stock.
paragraphs: Electricity supply remains unstable in several Malian regions even as conditions improve in the capital, Bamako. In Douentza, the town has been without power since Monday, 23 November, due to a fuel shortage, according to the local head of the energy agency. Similar persistent outages affect Macina in Ségou region and Ménaka in the north, where access has been irregular for over two years because of generator failures and supply difficulties.

The blackouts are disrupting economic activity and raising costs for small businesses. Oumar Ouologuem, a welder in Douentza, said buying diesel for his generator is financially difficult, though any electricity would help. Hawa Cissé, who sells traditional drinks like yogurt and ginger juice, reported losing merchandise that requires refrigeration. Moussa Dem, a member of civil society in Macina, warned that the lack of cold storage threatens food security and increases insecurity for fishmongers and butchers.

Authorities in Douentza stated that measures are underway to resupply the town with fuel in the coming days. Residents in these areas continue to call for durable solutions to the energy crisis, noting that women in rural areas rely heavily on electricity for income-generating activities.

ml.headline: Mali dengue tests cost up to 15 000 francs CFA in listed Bamako tariffs
ml.dek: Clinics say diagnosis requires a consultation and a timed test, and a negative result can lead to another sample.
paragraphs: Mali's health minister told the Council of Ministers on 18 November 2026 that confirmed dengue cases had risen compared with the previous week, but the communique gave no total. In Bamako, the PA&KA laboratory in Hamdallaye ACI 2000 lists a dengue test at 7 500 francs CFA with a one-day turnaround, and the Hôpital du Mali in Missabougou lists dengue serology at 15 000 francs CFA. The two methods may differ.

Oumou Coulibaly, a nurse at the Sabalibougou community health centre, said fever, headache and muscle pain can also signal malaria, so a consultation guides which tests to order. The reverse transcription polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR) and the NS1 test, which detects a viral protein, are most useful in the first week, while IgM serology, which detects antibodies, becomes useful after the seventh day. PA&KA says its prices rise by 20% during guard services and on public holidays.

Consultation, transport and prescribed care add to household costs. A negative NS1 or RT-PCR result can prompt the clinician to request a new sample. The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention says care should start without waiting for results when dengue is suspected.

ml.headline: Mali’s kidney congress highlights gaps in specialist care and prevention
ml.dek: The meeting cited five dialysis centres but said the country lacks operational peritoneal dialysis and kidney-transplant services.
paragraphs: Mali’s second International Congress of Nephrology opened in Bamako on Thursday, 26 November, bringing together African experts, researchers and technical partners to discuss chronic kidney disease. The meeting highlighted five dialysis centres in Bamako and the regions, alongside a dedicated master’s programme, and called for health services to adapt to rising non-communicable diseases.

Mali’s nephrology society president, Magara Samaké, said 60% of people in the country with chronic kidney failure are aged 20 to 40. The Global Kidney Health Atlas 2025 reports shortages of paediatric nephrologists and specialist surgeons, and says Mali has no operational peritoneal dialysis or kidney-transplant pathways.

The African nephrology association president cited a World Health Assembly resolution adopted on 10 February 2025 that calls for wider early screening, including creatinine and albuminuria tests, at local health facilities. The congress also identified organ transplantation and stronger national registers as priorities.

mr.headline: Mauritania starts 407 million-ouguiya upgrade of Boghé model farm
mr.dek: The project, financed by the International Development Association and the World Bank Group, will rehabilitate infrastructure and introduce modern irrigation.
paragraphs: Mauritanian President Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani laid the first stone on Thursday for a project to rehabilitate and expand the model farm serving Boghé, in Sarandougou village in the country’s southeast. The budget is 407 million and 737 000 new ouguiyas.

The Mauritanian News Agency said the work will cover more than 2 200 hectares and is financed by the International Development Association (IDA) and the World Bank Group. It includes repairing farm infrastructure and introducing modern irrigation techniques.

The agency said the project is intended to raise agricultural productivity, sustain resources and improve incomes for farmers in the Boghé region. El Ghazouani is visiting the Brakna region to oversee the launch and opening of development and service projects.

mr.headline: Mauritania's employment agency launches four job programmes
mr.dek: The agency also unveiled eight specialised services for groups including women, farm workers, students and Mauritanians living abroad.
paragraphs: Mauritania's National Employment Agency unveiled four job-integration programmes and eight specialised service offers in Nouakchott on Thursday, aiming to widen young people's job opportunities and match job seekers' skills to what employers need.

The programme TEAHIL (a qualifying training scheme that adapts job seekers' skills to labour-market requirements) and TEMHIR (which lets participants discover trades, become familiar with the workplace and gain field experience) are among the four. TED'IM combines training with work experience, while TEHFIZ, the employment incentive scheme, offers incentives to companies that hire job seekers.

The eight services target people with disabilities, madrasa graduates, young people who neither work nor study, women, would-be labour migrants, Mauritanians living abroad, farm workers and students. The agency said they form part of a wider modernisation of its system and the development of labour-market matching.

paragraphs: Mauritanian telecom company Mauritel opened a national network supervision centre on Thursday to monitor service performance, detect technical faults and coordinate repairs. mu.headline: Mauritius opens talks on 2027 wage compensation
mu.dek: Unions seek between Rs 1 200 and Rs 1 700, while employers urge restraint ahead of a government decision expected in December.
paragraphs: Mauritius opened tripartite consultations on Friday, 27 November, over wage compensation for 2027, with unions seeking between Rs 1 200 and Rs 1 700 and employers calling for moderation. Labour Minister Reza Uteem began the process with representatives of workers, employers and Statistics Mauritius at Victoria House in Port-Louis.

Statistics Mauritius was due to present the 2026 inflation rate at the technical meeting scheduled for 14 h 30. Uteem said the payment is an adjustment for lost purchasing power, not a salary revision, and that consultations would consider workers’ demands alongside businesses’ economic constraints.

Organisations have until Friday 4 December to submit written memorandums. Prime Minister Navin Ramgoolam is expected to chair a tripartite meeting in the second week of December, after which the finance minister will prepare a proposal for Cabinet approval. The Labour Ministry would then make regulations for payment from January 2027. A pension adjustment is also being considered.

mu.headline: Moody’s keeps Mauritius outlook negative, says upgrade unlikely soon
mu.dek: The agency wants sustained evidence of lower public debt and improved state finances before it considers stabilising its view.
paragraphs: Moody’s Ratings kept a negative outlook on Mauritius’s Baa3 sovereign rating, saying an upgrade was unlikely in the short term. The agency announced its position at a virtual press conference with GCR Ratings, a Moody’s subsidiary, on 26 November.

Raphaele Auberty, a Moody’s sovereign-risk official, said the outlook reflected uncertainty over the government’s ability to continue repairing public finances. The agency will watch public debt relative to gross domestic product and the primary balance, while assessing whether budget adjustments can be made without harming long-term growth.

Moody’s cited recent progress in fiscal consolidation, particularly during the last financial year, but said public debt remained a weakness. It does not recommend government policies; decisions on revenue and spending rest with Mauritian authorities.

mu.headline: Mauritius charges two former deputy governors over MIC hiring
mu.dek: The former officials are accused of favouring a CEO candidate; one also faces a charge over raising his monthly salary without board approval.
paragraphs: Mauritius’ Director of Public Prosecutions, Rashid Abdool Ahmine, filed a formal case on Thursday 26 November 2026 against former Bank of Mauritius Deputy Governors Hemlata Sadhna Sewraj-Gopal and Mardayah Kona Yerukunondu. The case is before the Supreme Court’s Financial Crimes Division and concerns the hiring of a chief executive for the Mauritius Investment Corporation (MIC).

The prosecution alleges the pair, who were also MIC directors, presented Jitendra Nathsing Bissessur to the board on 22 February 2021 as the top-ranked candidate. Sewraj-Gopal faces a second charge over signing a revised job offer on 4 March 2021, increasing Bissessur’s monthly salary from Rs 275 000 to Rs 325 000 without board approval. Prosecutors say this gave him an additional Rs 50 000 a month.
The charges are brought under sections 7(1) and 83 of the Prevention of Corruption Act 2002. The prosecution has listed nine witnesses.

mu.headline: Mauritius opens inquiry after inmate found dead at Melrose prison
mu.dek: The 52-year-old was found on his bed on 25 November, and drugs were later found under the bed and on partly burned paper.
paragraphs: Mauritius has opened an inquiry into the death of a 52-year-old prisoner found on his bed at Melrose prison on 25 November. A prison doctor who was called to the cell could only confirm the death.

Initial indications showed no signs of violence on the body. Closed-circuit television footage showed the man rolling a “ti-papie,” and Scene of Crime Office staff found partly burned paper with traces of a drug. A further search turned up drugs beneath the bed. He was serving a sentence in the Eastern High Security Prison for a drug case and was due for release in March 2027.
Investigators are working to determine the circumstances of the death. A separate report said a second prisoner died at Line Barracks within the same 24 hours, in different circumstances.

mz.headline: Mozambique’s 100 largest companies record 615 billion meticais in turnover
mz.dek: President Daniel Chapo announced the 2025 figure and called for reforms to improve the business environment.
paragraphs: Mozambique’s 100 largest companies recorded approximately 615 billion meticais (€8.7 billion) in turnover in 2025, President Daniel Chapo announced on Thursday. He also called for reforms to improve the business environment.

Chapo said the figures showed the strength and potential of Mozambique’s business sector, as well as the challenges it faces. The announcement covered the combined turnover of the 100 companies; it did not identify individual firms.
The president’s call for reform was the next step he set out, but no specific changes or timetable were given.

mz.headline: Trafigura names Helio Cumbi to lead Mozambique operations
mz.dek: The Mozambican executive will oversee the company’s energy, metals and minerals activities in the country and oil-business development across eastern and southern Africa.
paragraphs: Trafigura has named Helio Cumbi its executive director for Mozambique and put him in charge of developing its oil business across eastern and southern Africa. Cumbi, a Mozambican national with more than 15 years of experience in energy, infrastructure and investment, joins from ExxonMobil, where he was director for Africa and international financial institutions, based in the United States.

In his new role, Cumbi will oversee Trafigura’s work in Mozambique’s energy, metals and minerals sectors and lead engagement with commercial, institutional and government partners. He will also coordinate regional oil-business development. Trafigura said its group, including subsidiaries Puma Energy and Impala Terminals and a joint venture with IFM Investors, indirectly employs about 1,200 people in Mozambique.

Puma Energy runs 41 fuel stations and convenience stores and supplies seven airports and airfields in the country. Trafigura said it has operated in Mozambique for more than 20 years, supplying fuel and other commodities and supporting mining and metals through financing, offtake agreements and logistics.

mz.headline: Mozambique launches fashion council and sector mapping
mz.dek: The new council plans to map professionals, businesses and institutions as Maputo hosts a forum and fashion week from 7 to 12 December.
paragraphs: Maputo will host the Mozambique Fashion Forum from 7 to 8 December and the 21st Mozambique Fashion Week from 9 to 12 December, alongside the public launch of the Mozambique Fashion Council and a pop-up store. The programme brings together fashion, business and production groups to discuss links between creative work and the market.

The council’s first planned action is to map professionals, companies, institutions and organisations across the fashion sector, including designers, artisans, textile firms, schools, models and event promoters. The forum, organised with the Institute of Cotton and Oilseeds of Mozambique, will examine the chain from cotton and other raw materials through manufacturing, sales and exports.
The forum’s opening is scheduled for 9 a.m. on 7 December, with President Daniel Francisco Chapo due to attend. Participation is free with advance registration.

na.headline: Oceana reports 29% fall in Namibia horse mackerel catch
na.dek: Vessel surveys and late-year quota shortages cut fishing time, while average Rand selling prices climbed 18%.
paragraphs: Oceana Group reported that its Namibian horse mackerel catch and production fell 29% in the year ended 30 September. The company blamed longer planned surveys of both vessels in the second half, along with quota shortages late in the year that cut the days available for fishing.

Unit catch costs rose 5%, as smaller volumes and higher fuel costs on the unhedged share of supply pushed expenses up. Sales held steady at 42 216 tons, against 42 768 tons in 2025, the company said. Strong demand for affordable protein, especially smaller fish, lifted selling prices, which rose 18% in Rand terms even as the Rand gained 9% against the US dollar.

At group level, revenue slipped 4.2% to R9.6 billion, while profit after tax climbed 38.5% to R1,3 billion from R724 million in 2025, which Oceana credited to stronger operating performance and lower net interest expense.

na.headline: Bank Windhoek raises N$650 million through JSE note sale
na.dek: The three-year unsecured notes drew more than N$3.3 billion in bids and were priced 0.66 percentage points tighter than the bank’s previous bond listing.
paragraphs: Bank Windhoek raised N$650 million through a three-year senior unsecured note issuance on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange (JSE), after investors submitted more than N$3.3 billion in bids. The offer began at ZAR500 million, with an option to increase it to ZAR750 million.

The bank said demand within and below its price guidance allowed it to raise the funds at a lower cost than its previous bond listing. The notes were priced at the South African Rand Overnight Index Average (ZARONIA) plus 1.20%, 0.66 percentage points tighter than that earlier listing, according to the bank.
Managing director James Chapman said the bank would use diversified funding sources to support growth and manage funding costs.

na.headline: FNB Namibia warns digital banking growth is changing fraud risks
na.dek: Digital channels now carry most of the bank's transactions, and criminals are using artificial intelligence to make impersonation harder to spot.
paragraphs: Across FNB Namibia's customer base, the share of people using digital services has reached more than 92%, and digital channels now handle over 72% of its financial transactions. Amoré Nicholson, the bank's digital banking head, says that shift has made digital services part of everyday life in a geographically dispersed country.

Nicholson warns that fraudsters rely on urgent calls and messages that impersonate banks, pushing customers to approve transactions before they can think carefully. Artificial intelligence (AI) can reproduce voices and create convincing correspondence, making older advice such as checking for spelling errors less reliable.

The African Cyberthreat Assessment Report 2026 by INTERPOL (the International Criminal Police Organization) says AI enables 55% of reported cybercrime across Africa. Its global fraud assessment estimates that AI-assisted fraud is 4.5 times as profitable as conventional methods. Nicholson says banks must design security for customers who may be distracted or frightened.

na.headline: MTC commits N$135.6 million to sponsorships and social investment over three years
na.dek: The telecoms operator says its cumulative contribution to sponsorships and corporate social investment now stands at about N$420 million.
paragraphs: MTC, Namibia's telecommunications operator, has committed N$135.6 million over the next three years to sponsorships and corporate social investment (CSI). The commitment works out to N$45.2 million a year, of which N$30.38 million goes to sponsorship programmes, mostly in sport, and N$14.82 million to CSI funding.

The CSI money targets rural education, health, entrepreneurship, creative industries, environmental sustainability and community development. Managing Director Licky Erastus said the company's cumulative contribution to sponsorships and CSI now stands at about N$420 million, and that the aim is long-term change in communities across the country, not only compliance.

Erastus pointed to MTC's inaugural CSI Mukopano as a platform bringing together government, the private sector, civil society and community groups. Sophy Mouton of Hope Village thanked the company on behalf of sponsorship and CSI beneficiaries.

na.headline: Namibian police begin training 1 980 new cadets
na.dek: The recruits started on 1 November at three training centres after 2 050 cadet constables graduated in May and June.
paragraphs: The Namibian Police began training 1 980 new cadet constables on 1 November at three police training centres, Acting Inspector-General Major General Anne-Marie Nainda said. She spoke at the commemoration of the 36th anniversary of Police Day.

Nainda said the recruitment followed the graduation of 2 050 cadet constables in May and June this year. She said the new trainees were part of efforts to meet the force’s staffing needs and improve its ability to prevent and combat crime.

The force is also building or upgrading police facilities, while construction continues at Police Village in Babylon, Katutura, Epako Police Station in the Omaheke region and Greenwell Matango Police Station in the Zambezi region. The proposed Cybercrime Bill is intended to strengthen responses to offences committed through digital platforms and electronic systems.

ne.headline: Niamey requires permits for mosque construction and expansion
ne.dek: A November 17 order covers worship sites across all five municipal districts and gives existing sites six months to have their status reviewed.
paragraphs: Niamey's delegated city administrator, Col. Boubacar Soumana Garanké, signed an order on November 17 regulating the construction, expansion, renovation and occupation of land around mosques and other places of worship in the capital. It applies to mosques, prayer rooms, religious schools attached to worship sites and religious gathering spaces in all five municipal districts.

New construction, expansion or major changes require prior approval. Applicants must document land rights, submit technical plans and meet building, planning and safety rules. Permanent installations on sidewalks and roads are banned, as are obstructions to drains, traffic routes and property access. The order also requires a census of existing worship sites; managers have six months from publication to have their sites reviewed by the relevant services.
Violations can lead to work being suspended, unauthorised installations removed, public land cleared and fines imposed under existing rules.

ne.headline: Niger shows investors sites for two proposed industrial zones
ne.dek: Yawaré covers 250 hectares and Bougoum 2421 hectares; the government is discussing investment with forum participants and Turkey.
paragraphs: Niger’s commerce and industry minister, Abdoulaye Seydou, led investors to proposed industrial sites at Yawaré and Bougoum near Niamey on 26 November. The visit took place during the International Forum “Invest in Niger,” held in Niamey from 24 to 26 November.

Seydou said Yawaré covers 250 hectares and Bougoum 2421 hectares. The government has listed both developments among 30 priority projects presented to domestic and foreign investors, and is discussing them with forum participants who expressed interest in setting up industrial units, as well as with Turkey at an institutional level.

The government is also pursuing a process for Bougoum to qualify for an industrialisation facilitation mechanism for least developed countries. Seydou said the special economic zone is intended to produce goods for export as well as domestic production.

ne.headline: Niger completes two wholesale markets in Diffa region
ne.dek: The markets in Goudoumaria and Mainé-Soroa have received provisional acceptance, while supervision continued on two roads toward Nigeria.
paragraphs: Niger has completed wholesale markets in Goudoumaria and Mainé-Soroa, in the Diffa region, after construction works received provisional acceptance. Mamane Gouzaé, Diffa’s deputy secretary-general, inspected the facilities on Wednesday, 25 November, during a visit to projects funded by the Lake Chad Region Recovery and Development Project (PROLAC-Niger).

The markets are intended to improve sales of agricultural products and other goods and ease trade among producers, merchants and consumers. Gouzaé said the contractors had met their commitments and praised the pace of work.

The inspection also covered two laterite-road routes toward Nigeria: Goudoumaria to Kodjiméri and Abuja, spanning 45.898 kilometres, and Djajéri-Chéri-Boula Toura, spanning 36.620 kilometres. The project says the roads are intended to improve rural access, mobility and cross-border trade.
